title: Availability fallback rehearsal and handoff — 42-day plan
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc sketches a practical 42-day cross-functional plan to validate our availability fallback strategies and SLO handoff for model-serving features. Goal: reduce likelihood of customer-visible downtime during partial outages by exercising fallback routing, degraded-model pathways, and operational handoffs so feature teams can pass SLO acceptance criteria with clear runbooks.

Why this is different from a generic SLO rollout: we focus on rehearsing the behavior under real operational constraints (quota limits, KV-cache stale state, token-batching mismatches) and on making the human handoff crisp between oncall, feature owners, and platform.

High-level objectives (measurable):
- Run 3 staged rehearsals that simulate region outage, model-variant exhaustion, and degraded-kv-cache corruption.
- Each rehearsal: < 2% user error-rate increase above baseline (target), and recovery within 10 minutes to a functional degraded mode.
- Document a one-page fallback runbook per feature team and ship it to the Console runbook library.
- Update SLO acceptance checklist and gating to include fallback test sign-off.

Scope (in/out):
In-scope:
- Hosted inference routes and Dedicated fallback paths (same API surface)
- Routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, and region-prefer
- Model variants with quantized/backoff options (v1, v1-quant, v0.9)
- Oncall activation and runbook handoff for 30 minutes post-failure
Out-of-scope:
- Large re-architecture changes to serving runtime kernels
- Long-term capacity expansion (we'll create follow-up tickets)

Stakeholders and owners:
- SRE lead: Maya Chen (owner) — overall plan and rehearsal cadence
- Platform eng: Diego Ramirez — implements simulated failpoints and metrics hooks
- Feature owners: Priya Patel, Jordan Lee — provide two critical routes each for rehearsal
- Developer-ex (docs + Console): Hannah Wu — runbook templates + publishing
- Incident commander rota: Liam O'Connor + oncall rotation volunteers

Deliverables (artifact list):
- Rehearsal scripts (git): infra/test/rehearsals/availability/* — implements chaos scenarios
- Per-route fallback runbook (one-pager) — Console link + markdown in repo
- Updated SLO acceptance checklist (doc) — adds rehearsal sign-off items
- Post-rehearsal retro notes and action tickets (Jira list)

42-day timeline (phases):
Phase 0: Prep (days 0–7)
- Day 0–2: Stakeholder sync, identify 6 routes (3 platform, 3 product).
- Day 3–5: Platform implements feature flags for failpoints and synthetic load harnesses.
- Day 6–7: Docs team drafts runbook template; SRE defines rehearsal pass/fail metrics.

Phase 1: Lab rehearsals (days 8–21) — low-risk simulated environment
- Week 2: Two lab rehearsals run against a staging cluster. Scenarios: region failover + model-variant swap.
- Deliverable: per-route obs checklist (dashboards, alerts) + time-to-degraded-mode measurement.

Phase 2: Canary rehearsals (days 22–35) — small % of production traffic
- Week 4: Canary at 1–3% of traffic for routes marked low-risk. Test throttling to model-variants and observe client impact.
- Oncall present; incident commander will decide escalation.

Phase 3: Full-scale rehearsal & handoff (days 36–42)
- Day 36–38: Run full production-rehearsal window with coordinated comms. Feature teams and SRE staff in war room.
- Day 39–42: Postmortem, close action items, add fallback sign-off to SLO gating.

Rehearsal scenarios (concrete):
1) Region failover: Simulate control-plane loss in region-us-west-2 for 8 minutes. Validate smart routing shifts to us-east-1, ensure model-variant compatibility, KV-caches warm in < 4 minutes.
2) Model-variant exhaustion: Exhaust quota on v1 and validate automatic fallback to v1-quant with degraded-quality notice header and telemetry.
3) KV cache corruption: Inject a stale prefix scenario that causes cache misses for a subset of requests to see latency SLO impact and rollout of prefix-based cache-bypass.
4) Autoscaler lag: Force an autoscaler scaling delay to exercise burst-capacity policy and fallback to reserved capacity.

Acceptance criteria per rehearsal (pass/fail):
- Functional: error-rate for exercised routes <= baseline + 5 percentage points during first 2 minutes, <= baseline + 2 points within 10 minutes.
- Latency: p95 increase <= 2x baseline for degraded-mode; p50 within 20% of baseline.
- Stability: no unplanned rollbacks of routing policies.
- Operational: runbook steps executed; oncall handoff completed and documented in post-incident notes.

Dashboards and telemetry to prepare (owners):
- Service health dashboard: error-rate, p50/p95 latency, token throughput — Platform (Diego)
- Routing decisions log: per-request routing reason tag (latency/cost/region) — Platform (Diego)
- Fallback metrics: counts of fallback events, duration, model-variant swaps — Feature owners
- Error-budget burn timeline overlay for each route — SRE (Maya)

Communications and war-room playbook:
- Pre-notice to customers: outbound only for rehearsals that touch >1% traffic; drafted by customer-success.
- Internal comms: #reliability-exercises, daily summary in Confluence page.
- War room: Zoom + live doc with checklist. Incident commander leads, owner of route provides feature context.

Runbook one-pager template (what to include):
- Trigger conditions (alert thresholds)
- Quick triage (what telemetry to inspect first)
- Rollback vs degrade decision tree
- How to trigger automatic fallback and manual override steps
- Communication checklist (who to ping)
- Post-event steps and evidence to capture

Handoff checklist (for sign-off):
- Feature owner confirms runbook in Console
- Platform verifies metrics and routing-logs instrumentation
- SRE signs off that rehearsals pass acceptance criteria twice in a row
- Product/CS accepts customer-facing note (if needed)

Risks and mitigations (open):
- Risk: Canary rehearsals might expose latent bugs in client SDKs. Mitigation: start with synthetic clients and explicit client-owner opt-in.
- Risk: Cascading failures in autoscaler. Mitigation: schedule small blast radius and require policy guardrails.
- Risk: False-positive alerts during rehearsal. Mitigation: tag rehearsal events in observability and mute noisy alerts temporarily with clear timestamps.

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
- Q1: Which 6 routes provide the most meaningful coverage? (Priya to propose by day 2)
- Q2: Do we need formal customer notice templates for 1% canaries? (CS + Legal)
- TODO: Diego to add routing-reason tag instrumentation (due day 5)
- TODO: Hannah to create and publish runbook template (due day 7)

Post-rehearsal artifacts and next steps:
- Create tickets for any action items discovered (owner & SLA for fix)
- Add fallback rehearsal sign-off to onboarding checklist for new feature launches
- Quarterly replay: schedule the same rehearsal cadence every quarter and rotate route ownership to broaden coverage

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep rehearsals small and iterated — we learn faster if we can fail forward quickly
- Emphasize human handoff clarity; the biggest friction is confusion about who owns next steps after automatic fallback triggers
- Try to capture a short video of the war-room timeline for asynchronous review

Appendix: quick rehearsal script example (lab):
- Step 0: Flip feature flag to enable failpoint for route X in staging
- Step 1: Start synthetic load (clients simulate diverse seq lengths) for 5 minutes
- Step 2: Induce model-variant quota exhaustion for v1 (block v1 allocations)
- Step 3: Observe fallback to v1-quant for 3 minutes, collect latency and token counts
- Step 4: Revert failpoint, verify traffic flows back and caches re-warm

If you want to move forward: I recommend we run the stakeholder kickoff this week, lock the six routes, and have Diego/Hannah do a quick smoke test in staging by day 5.

— Maya
